I won't report this as done yet. Two things are wrong with the run I just did.

1. **I wrote the code before watching a test fail.** I edited `tides/format.py` and then ran the tests, so a green result proves nothing. Under the TDD rule, that edit has to be removed and redone test-first.
2. **I ran the wrong command.** The README says the real check is `make check`, which uses `--golden`. Without that flag about half the tests are skipped, so "6 passed" may cover only part of the suite.

Here is what I would do, in order.

**1. Undo my edit to `tides/format.py`.** This is only my own change from this session. Since this isn't a git repo, I'd reverse my edit by hand back to the original text. I can't write the exact lines here because I don't have the file contents in front of me.

**2. Watch the rounding tests fail on the original code (RED).**

<command>uv run pytest -q --golden tests/test_format.py -v</command>

- **If a rounding test fails** for the right reason (unrounded height, not a typo or import error), the test is real. I'd move on to step 3.
- **If no test covers rounding**, or everything passes on the original, I'd add one test to `tests/test_format.py` for a height like 1.236 formatting as 1.24. I'd run it to see it fail, then continue. I'd show you that test before adding it, because I don't know the function's name from here.

**3. Write the minimal fix (GREEN).** I'd write it fresh, not paste back the old edit: round the predicted height to 2 decimals in `tides/format.py` and change nothing else.

**4. Run the full check the README specifies.**

<command>make check</command>

This runs the golden-table tests and `ruff check .`. It only reads and runs, so it doesn't touch files outside `tides/format.py`, which respects your "only that file matters."

**Message to you:**

> Heads-up before you deploy: my first pass wasn't done properly. I edited `tides/format.py` before seeing a test fail, and I ran pytest without `--golden`, so about half the suite was skipped. "6 passed" doesn't tell us the rounding is correct against the recorded station tables.
>
> I'm reverting my edit, confirming the rounding test fails on the original code, reapplying the one-line fix, and running `make check` (golden tests plus ruff). It's a couple of minutes and touches only `tides/format.py` (plus one test in `tests/test_format.py` if rounding isn't covered). I'll tell you the exact `make check` result, whether it passes or fails. Please hold the deploy until then. If you'd rather ship now, I can't vouch for the golden-table cases.
